scope: Local origin and reverse-tunnel resource transfer; not a public-site latency benchmark

method.measurement: Sum of PerformanceResourceTiming.transferSize for page subresources, excluding the main HTML document
method.baseline: Existing unchanged Node processes on ports 3000 and 8000, through isolated loopback proxies
method.optimized: New app and H5 static server on temporary loopback ports, without rebuilding H5
method.adminApi: Synthetic loopback responses; no production business API calls
method.h5Identity: Guest; no owner login or payment
method.cache: Fresh browser context for cold load, same-context navigation for warm load; browser routing was not used because it disables HTTP cache

boundaries.html: no-store; warm admin HTML component requests intentionally transfer fresh bodies instead of the previous 304 behavior
boundaries.hashedJsAndCss: private, max-age=31536000, immutable only after gateway authentication, with matching static MIME, 200 or 304 status and no Set-Cookie
boundaries.otherTextAssets: private, no-cache with ETag and Last-Modified; gateway continues to force no-store
boundaries.gzipCache: At most 64 compressed entries and 8 MiB retained compressed data per static server; eligible individual files at most 2 MiB. The 8 MiB cap does not include pending file reads, zlib work buffers or process memory; concurrent cold requests can use more memory.
boundaries.directoryLinks: Canonical real paths are verified before text delivery and binary/Range fallback; an escaping symlink or Windows junction returns 403/no-store
boundaries.fallback: Existing static implementation handles binary files, Range requests and directory behavior

limitations: Public nginx already enabled gzip before this change. Local compression reduces traffic before the SSH tunnel and avoids repeatedly recompressing unchanged assets; these numbers must not be described as a public-network speedup of the same percentage.
Admin already had validators, so the main gain is cold-load compression. Its warm transfer rises slightly because HTML is now explicitly no-store.
Images retain existing caching behavior. H5 warm-load savings come from the five immutable JS/CSS chunks.
Measurements use synthetic admin responses and guest H5. They do not establish production concurrent-user capacity or authenticated business latency.
Running services must be restarted separately to activate these source changes. This verification did not restart the existing services.
